idea-plugin.name: Grok Build By Kafei
idea-plugin.description:
Grok Build is an IntelliJ chat for the xAI Grok agent. It uses the same WebView UI and ACP grok agent stdio core as the VS Code extension, hosted with JCEF and a Node sidecar. Requires Node.js and the Grok CLI.

IntelliJ 版 Grok Build：与 VS Code 插件共用同一套 WebView UI 和 Agent 核心。

  • Chat, login, API key, models, effort, Ask / Plan / Default modes
  • Grok Diff review and revert
  • Sessions, compact, rewind, fork, export, usage
  • Rules, skills, MCP, agents, worktrees, memory, marketplace
  • Add editor selection or the active file as context
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Grok Build By Kafei 0.2.32: compatibility range 2025.2–2026.3 (since-build 252, until-build 263.*).

0.2.32 — Remote review opens each changed file as a workspace tab. The chat no longer jumps to the top: the transcript stays in place instead of being moved into the workspace shell.

0.2.31 — Reviews use histogram anchors plus Myers on the gaps, computed on the host and clipped before the web page. Opening review no longer jumps the chat to the top.

0.2.30 — Remote web no longer jumps the chat to the top when clicking buttons. Reviews of a few hundred edits no longer open as a 4000-line rewrite.

0.2.29 — Remote web uses thin rounded overlay scrollbars. Sending a message no longer jumps the chat to the top.

0.2.28 — Small edits no longer show as thousands of lines. The host computes review diffs and sends each file to the remote page separately.

0.2.27 — Remote workspace: explorer create/rename/delete, larger saves, no error banners. Large reviews no longer freeze the page.

0.2.26 — Remote workspace uses Monaco with Shiki TextMate highlighting.

0.2.25 — Remote workspace opens files in a top tab bar so several files can stay open at once.

0.2.24 — Remote web opens immediately on a long chat: the first frame is small, then history arrives in chunks instead of one giant snapshot.

0.2.23 — Remote web blocks pinch-zoom, keeps the sidebar/workspace switch compact, connects the chat without a refresh after pairing, and resizes panes without hitching.

0.2.22 — Remote review opens in the center editor, not a fullscreen overlay. The explorer lists the project files. The browser no longer spins after pairing when the IDE is already in chat. Pane widths are dragged; collapse controls are gone.

0.2.21 — Remote workspace explorer indexes one folder at a time. Pairing no longer shows a red 0 or “already in use” after a successful login.

0.2.20 — Remote workspace matches VS Code: explorer | editor | original chat sidebar, with draggable splits. Opening a file always re-syncs it from the computer.

0.2.19 — Remote web adds sidebar and workspace views. Workspace has a foldable explorer and editor for reading, small edits, and review. Phones can attach photos and files; review and file preview no longer depend on the IDE window.

0.2.18 — Remote web: menus stay inside the screen, the session reconnects after a drop, pairing can use a saved password, and review/file preview work in the browser.

0.2.17 — Public remote is a single on/off switch that uses the built-in relay. The pairing page no longer tells HTTP users to drop https.

0.2.16 — One plugin allows one browser. The default VPS can relay many plugins at once by assigning each a free public port. Pairing codes cannot be stacked.

0.2.15 — Remote access splits LAN and public. Public mode dials your VPS with an SSH reverse tunnel and issues one pairing code per person.

0.2.14 — iPad/Safari LAN remote: the pairing token is put on the WebSocket URL so the session can open without cookies.

0.2.13 — LAN remote access: a pairing-code page in Settings starts an HTTP/WebSocket server so a browser can open the same chat.

0.2.12 — Long streams throttle Markdown paints so the IDE stays responsive. GitHub start:end:path fences no longer swallow later headings.

0.2.11 — Long streaming replies render Markdown as HTML instead of dumping raw pipes and hashes.

0.2.10 — Model and effort dropdowns sit on glass layer 4 and open above the composer.

0.2.9 — Markdown tables, inline code, the edits bar, and file chips are frosted glass like the rest of the chrome.

0.2.8 — Glass chrome gets a 1px white edge, top highlight, and drop shadow. Component blur is a separate slider from wallpaper blur.

0.2.7 — The blur slider only changes the wallpaper. Bubbles, cards, and menus always frost what is behind them.

0.2.6 — Wallpaper stays sharp and is only adjusted in settings. Every chrome piece frosts a clipped copy of the wallpaper; higher layers blur more.

0.2.5 — Hierarchical frost actually blurs: wallpaper is filtered on the plate; bubbles and menus add stronger backdrop-filter on top.

0.2.4 — Frost is blur-only: no tinted overlay. Layered backdrop-filter from plate through inner menus.

0.2.3 — Seven-layer frost: wallpaper, plate, bubbles, header buttons, more-menu, drawers/settings, then inner menus.

0.2.2 — Frosted glass on every bubble, card, and chip: each piece blurs only its own rectangle.

0.2.1 — Login can be skipped. Optional frosted glass on cards and buttons.

0.2.0 — Louder notification chime. Wallpaper preview, video wallpaper, and turn-complete sounds.

0.1.114 — Wallpaper preview restores pan and zoom as soon as it opens, without nudging the slider.

0.1.113 — Notification chime is louder.

0.1.112 — Optional chime when a turn finishes or is interrupted.

0.1.111 — IDEA wallpaper videos: stage next to the chat page; transcode H.264 to WebM when ffmpeg is installed.

0.1.110 — Wallpaper zoom goes to 800% and always keeps the original aspect ratio.

0.1.109 — Wallpaper accepts looping videos (mp4, webm) and the full-window preview pans and centers them.

0.1.108 — Wallpaper preview is a full-window editor: click to set the center, drag to pan, at the current viewport size.

0.1.107 — Settings, history, and dashboard drawers actually frost-blur the home/chat behind them.

0.1.106 — One frost plate on home/chat; settings and drawers blur that main page. Less backdrop-filter jank.

0.1.105 — Keep wallpaper mounted when restoring a session; glass blur is adjustable.

0.1.104 — Home uses the same floating sheet as chat; more-menu stacks above the composer; glass opacity is adjustable.

0.1.103 — Theme panel style: frosted glass or a solid floating sheet; wallpaper can be panned and zoomed.

0.1.102 — Theme wallpaper: Grok icon or a custom image, with opacity, background color in the gaps, and center-crop when the image is larger than the chat.

0.1.101 — Drag workspace files onto the chat to attach them as references.

0.1.100 — Custom endpoints accept a max context window, including 128k-style values.

0.1.99 — Confirming an edited user message actually resends it (editUserPrompt was dropped by the host).

0.1.98 — Do not freeze the IDE on first open: show the tool window first, start Chromium on the next frame, and do not pre-warm a second Diff browser.

0.1.97 — Plugin Verifier: drop internal PluginManagerCore, deprecated ReadAction.compute, and override-only ActionGroup.getChildren.

0.1.96 — Pre-warm the Grok Diff browser so the first Review is a tab switch, not a JCEF cold start.

0.1.95 — Review clicks hop off the JCEF thread onto the EDT so Grok Diff can open.

0.1.94 — Grok Diff opens as a center editor tab; open-buffer reads/writes go through IntelliJ documents.

0.1.93 — Stop re-serializing the active file on every keystroke; coalesce JCEF stream paints.

0.1.92 — IntelliJ 2026.2: optional Web Browser (JCEF) dependency so the chat tool window can load.

0.1.89 — Marketplace Plugin Verifier: claim only the IntelliJ builds this binary is compiled against.

0.1.88 — Cancelled and leftover steps stay on the card and render muted instead of as errors.

0.1.87 — Full host rewrite: every VS Code command, live editor context, IntelliJ theme, status bar, settings, Grok Diff, terminal.
